Prerequisite: The FortiGate registered to FortiCare in a FortiCloud account, with a valid FortiCare support contract that includes Firmware & General Updates (FMWR)
What it enables: Access to the GUI and the full CLI on models that enforce registration, upgrades to a new major or minor FortiOS release and firmware downloads from FortiGuard, and the FMWR definitions: application control signatures (including the generative AI database), virtual patch signatures for local-in policies, inline CASB application definitions, the Internet Service Database, and PSIRT vulnerability definitions
How to put it in place: Register the FortiGate and its contracts on the FortiCloud support portal (in an air-gapped network, upload the license file in the setup wizard), then check the entitlements and expiry dates in GUI: System > FortiGuard
Source: FortiOS 7.4.0 NFG, "Update FortiGuard License Information widget" (License Information widget: Firmware & General Updates and FortiCare Support entitlements), "Prevent FortiGates with an expired support contract from upgrading to a major or minor firmware release", "Prevent firmware upgrade depending on the current firmware license's expiration date", "Required firmware upgrades for FortiGate appliances with invalid support contracts or that have reached EOES", and "Add inline CASB security profile"; FortiOS 7.6.0 NFG, "Enforce FortiCare registration after new GUI login", "Enforce FortiCare registration with read-only CLI", and "Application control support for generative AI" (database updates require an FMWR contract)

Prerequisite: A path from the FortiGate to the FortiGuard Distribution Network: DNS and a route to the FortiGuard servers with the traffic allowed outbound, or an upstream proxy or custom override servers (such as FortiManager), and FortiGuard anycast where a feature needs it
What it enables: Signature, engine, and package updates, web filter and DNS filter rating queries, URL risk scores, virtual patching queries to the FortiGuard API, zero-day malware stream scanning, automatic firmware upgrade checks, the end-of-support and time zone packages, and reports of unauthorized firmware modification
How to put it in place: Allow the FortiGuard traffic outbound, or set a proxy with config system fortiguard; set proxy-server-ip <PROXY_IP>; set proxy-server-port <PORT>; end; turn on anycast with config system fortiguard; set fortiguard-anycast enable; end; server preference in GUI: System > FortiGuard
Source: FortiOS 8.0.0 NFG, "Enhanced FortiGuard server selection and load balancing" and "Configurable FQDN Host header for FortiGate proxy communication"; FortiOS 7.6.0 NFG, "Zero-day malware stream scanning" (FortiGuard Anycast must be enabled), "Introduce URL risk-scores in determining policy action", and "Streamline timezone updates with a downloadable database"; FortiOS 7.2.0 NFG, "Virtual patching on the local-in management interface" and "Support checking for firmware updates daily when auto firmware upgrade is enabled"; FortiOS 7.4.0 NFG, "Display warnings for supported Fabric devices passing their hardware EOS date" and "Unauthorized firmware modification attempt reporting"

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard Intrusion Prevention (IPS) subscription
What it enables: IPS definitions and engine updates, malicious URL and botnet IP and domain lists, the AI/Machine Learning IPS Definitions package (AI and ML-based IPS detection and DNS tunneling detection), and, on 7.2.4 and 7.2.5, virtual patching on the local-in interface
How to put it in place: Purchase the subscription, register it to the FortiGate (P1), and check it in GUI: System > FortiGuard
Source: FortiOS 7.4.0 NFG, "Update FortiGuard License Information widget" (Intrusion Prevention entitlement); FortiOS 7.6.0 NFG, "AI and ML-based IPS detection" (devices with an active IPS subscription); FortiOS 8.0.0 NFG, "Enhanced DNS security with AI and ML driven threat detection" (an active IPS subscription is required); FortiOS 7.2.0 NFG, "Virtual patching on the local-in management interface" (valid IPS license, changed in 7.2.6 and 7.4.1)

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard Advanced Malware Protection (antivirus) subscription
What it enables: Antivirus definitions and engine updates, the AI malware detection model, mobile malware definitions, and outbreak prevention hash queries for antivirus profiles
How to put it in place: Purchase the subscription, register it to the FortiGate (P1), and check it in GUI: System > FortiGuard
Source: FortiOS 7.4.0 NFG, "Update FortiGuard License Information widget" (Advanced Malware Protection entitlement); FortiOS 7.0.0 NFG, "AI-based malware detection" (devices with an active AV subscription)

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard Web Filtering (Web Security) subscription
What it enables: FortiGuard categories in web filter, DNS filter, and video filter profiles, URL risk scores, and the malicious certificate database (blocked certificates in SSL/SSH inspection and the client certificate blocklist of the secure explicit proxy)
How to put it in place: Purchase the subscription, register it to the FortiGate (P1), and check it in GUI: System > FortiGuard
Source: FortiOS 7.4.0 NFG, "Update FortiGuard License Information widget" (Web Filtering entitlement: the Web Security service); FortiOS 7.6.0 NFG, "Introduce URL risk-scores in determining policy action" (FortiGuard URL rating service); FortiOS 8.0.0 NFG, "Secure explicit proxy with client certificate blocklist enforcement" (an active FortiGuard subscription is required to use the Malicious Certificate Database)

Prerequisite: A FortiGate model with a log disk (local disk storage)
What it enables: Local disk logging, the policy change audit trail, log upload from disk, and quarantined files (which also work with FortiAnalyzer logging)
How to put it in place: Check that get system status reports the log hard disk as available
Source: FortiOS 7.2.0 NFG, "Add Policy change summary and Policy expiration to Workflow Management" (the Audit Trail is only supported by FortiGate models with disk logging); FortiOS 7.4.0 NFG, "Download quarantined files in archive format" (disk logging capacity or FortiAnalyzer); FortiOS 8.0.0 NFG, "Secure log upload enhancements with SFTP and LZ4 support"; get system status output in the NFGs (Log hard disk: Available or Not available)

Prerequisite: Preparation for FIPS-CC mode: a maintenance window, because enabling the mode reboots the FortiGate and leaving FIPS cipher mode needs a factory reset; on cloud FortiGate VMs, all VPN configurations removed before the mode is enabled
What it enables: FIPS-CC mode on appliances, and FIPS cipher mode on FortiGate VMs in public clouds
How to put it in place: Schedule the change, back up the configuration, and on a cloud VM remove the VPN configuration first and re-create it after the mode is enabled
Source: FortiOS 7.0.0 NFG, "FIPS cipher mode for OCI and GCP FortiGate VMs" (all VPN configurations must be removed; a factory reset is required to disable it); FortiOS 7.4.0 NFG, "Add built-in entropy source" (enabling FIPS-CC mode causes the FortiGate to reboot); FortiOS 7.2.0 NFG, "AWS silent fips-cipher enablement"

Prerequisite: The DoD PKI root and intermediate CA certificates (and those of any other approved CA) imported into the FortiGate
What it enables: Validation of administrator, user, and VPN peer certificates, and of the certificates of servers and Fabric devices the FortiGate connects to (LDAPS, certificate-authorized Fabric members)
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Certificates (Import, CA Certificate)
Source: Chapter row "CA certificates (DoD-approved CAs)"; FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, "config user peer" (ca) and "config user ldap" (ca-cert); FortiOS 8.0.0 NFG, "Enhancement to certificate authorization for Security Fabric devices" (the issuer must be a trusted CA)

Prerequisite: A certificate issued to the FortiGate by the DoD PKI (from a certificate signing request) and imported as a local certificate
What it enables: The HTTPS administration server certificate, IPsec signature authentication, the secure explicit proxy, and the client certificate for LDAPS servers that require one
How to put it in place: Generate a certificate signing request, have the DoD PKI sign it, and import the signed certificate in GUI: System > Certificates
Source: Chapter rows "Local certificate wizard" and "New default certificate for HTTPS administrative access"; FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, "config vpn ipsec phase1-interface" (certificate) and "config user ldap" (client-cert); FortiOS 7.2.0 NFG, "Configuring client certificate authentication on the LDAP server"

Prerequisite: A DoD-issued subordinate CA certificate and key for SSL deep inspection, imported into the FortiGate, with its issuing CA in the trusted certificate store of every client
What it enables: SSL deep inspection without certificate warnings, and the features that need deep inspection: HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 inspection, DNS over TLS and HTTPS inspection, Encrypted Client Hello control, video filtering, and inline CASB
How to put it in place: Deploy the issuing CA to the client trust stores, import the certificate in GUI: System > Certificates (Import, Local Certificate), and select it with config firewall ssl-ssh-profile; edit <PROFILE>; set caname <CA_CERT>; next; end
Source: FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, "config firewall ssl-ssh-profile" (caname); FortiOS 7.0.0 NFG, "Video filtering" (requires SSL deep inspection); FortiOS 7.4.0 NFG, "Add inline CASB security profile" (proxy-based inspection with a deep inspection SSL profile)

Prerequisite: DoD CRL distribution points or OCSP responders reachable from the FortiGate, with CRL updates or OCSP checks configured
What it enables: Revocation checks of administrator, user, VPN peer, and server certificates
How to put it in place: config vpn certificate crl; edit <CRL>; set http-url <CRL_URL>; set update-interval <SECONDS>; next; end; or config vpn certificate setting; set ocsp-status enable; set ocsp-default-server <OCSP_SERVER>; end
Source: FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, "config vpn certificate crl" (http-url, update-interval) and "config vpn certificate setting" (ocsp-status, ocsp-default-server)

Prerequisite: DoD PKI certificates (such as the CAC) issued to the users and endpoints, with the middleware that presents them
What it enables: Client certificate authentication for SSL VPN, dial-up IPsec VPN, the access proxy, and the secure explicit proxy, and LDAP- or RADIUS-integrated certificate authentication
How to put it in place: Issued by the DoD PKI; not a FortiGate setting
Source: FortiOS 7.0.0 NFG, "mTLS client certificate authentication" (clients are issued certificates by the CA); FortiOS 7.4.0 NFG, "IPsec IKEv2 VPN 2FA with EAP and certificate authentication" and "RADIUS integrated certificate authentication for SSL VPN"; FortiOS 7.2.0 NFG, "Specify the SAN field to use for LDAP-integrated certificate authentication"

Prerequisite: An LDAP directory server reachable over LDAPS, with a bind account and the user and group objects
What it enables: Remote administrator authentication with LDAP (and the restriction of local administrator logins while the server is reachable), user groups with remote members, and LDAP-integrated certificate authentication
How to put it in place: Create the bind account on the directory, then test with diagnose test authserver ldap <LDAP_SERVER> <USER> <PASSWORD>
Source: FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, "config user ldap"; FortiOS 7.2.0 NFG, "Improve admin-restrict-local handling of multiple authentication servers"; FortiOS 7.6.0 NFG, "Restrict local administrator logins through the console"

Prerequisite: A syslog server that accepts reliable syslog over TLS
What it enables: Remote syslog of FortiGate logs, and the health check that alerts when the syslog server stops responding
How to put it in place: Configure the server for TLS on the reliable syslog port; not a FortiGate setting
Source: FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, "config log syslogd setting" (mode reliable, enc-algorithm); chapter row "Logging to syslog servers over reliable TLS"

Prerequisite: A FortiAnalyzer that has authorized the FortiGate (7.0.1 or later for authorization from the Fabric connector); for an alternate FortiAnalyzer, FortiAnalyzers in geo-redundant HA mode
What it enables: Encrypted, reliable, real-time logging to FortiAnalyzer, its log caching, and switching to an alternate FortiAnalyzer
How to put it in place: Authorize the device on the FortiAnalyzer, then check with execute log fortianalyzer test-connectivity
Source: FortiOS 7.0.0 NFG, "Simplify Fabric approval workflow for FortiAnalyzer" (FortiAnalyzer 7.0.1 is required); FortiOS 7.4.0 NFG, "Support switching to an alternate FortiAnalyzer if the main FortiAnalyzer is unavailable" (geo-redundant HA mode)

Prerequisite: An SMTP server that accepts mail from the FortiGate, and the mailbox of the ISSO and SA
What it enables: Email actions of automation stitches (alerts on audit and log failure events)
How to put it in place: config system email-server; set server <SMTP_SERVER>; set port <PORT>; set security smtps; end
Source: FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, "config system email-server" and "config system automation-action" (action-type email)

Prerequisite: Authoritative NTP servers (two or more) with authentication keys shared with the FortiGate
What it enables: Authenticated, redundant time synchronization
How to put it in place: Agree on the key ID and key with the NTP server administrator; check with diagnose sys ntp status
Source: FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, "config system ntp" (ntpserver: authentication, key, key-id); chapter row "NTP with authenticated, redundant servers"

Prerequisite: An SNMPv3 manager with the matching user, authentication, and privacy settings
What it enables: SNMPv3 queries and traps, including queries from non-management VDOMs
How to put it in place: Configure the user on the manager, and list it as a notify host with config system snmp user; edit <NAME>; set notify-hosts <MANAGER_IP>; next; end
Source: FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, "config system snmp user"; FortiOS 7.2.0 NFG, "Access control for SNMP based on the MIB-view and VDOM"; FortiOS 7.6.0 NFG, "Non-management VDOMs perform queries using SNMP v3"

Prerequisite: The administrator profile that an account will use
What it enables: Least-privilege local, remote, and REST API administrator accounts
How to put it in place: config system accprofile; edit <PROFILE>; set sysgrp read; next; end; or GUI: System > Admin Profiles
Source: Chapter row "Administrator profiles: System access permission"; FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, "config system accprofile"

Prerequisite: A user group whose members are the remote authentication server (or its groups)
What it enables: Remote administrators matched on a server group, and user authentication groups for dial-up VPN
How to put it in place: config user group; edit <GROUP>; set member <LDAP_SERVER>; next; end; or GUI: User & Authentication > User Groups
Source: Chapter row "User groups with remote (LDAP) servers"; FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, "config user group"

Prerequisite: A dedicated management interface on a separate management network, with address objects for the management hosts
What it enables: Administrative access, local-in policies, DoS policies, and trusted hosts limited to the management network, and policies that keep management traffic off other networks
How to put it in place: config firewall address; edit <MGMT_HOSTS>; set subnet <IP> <MASK>; next; end; interface settings in GUI: Network > Interfaces
Source: Chapter rows "Administrative access protocols on each interface" and "Local-in policies (traffic to the FortiGate itself)"; FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, "config firewall address"

Prerequisite: An IPsec VPN tunnel (phase 1 interface) to the peer
What it enables: Phase 2 selectors, policies for traffic from VPN interfaces, and the tunnel features (serial number exchange, cross-validation, post-quantum and QKD key exchange)
How to put it in place: config vpn ipsec phase1-interface; edit <TUNNEL>; set interface <PORT>; set remote-gw <PEER_IP>; next; end; or GUI: VPN > IPsec Tunnels
Source: Chapter row "IPsec VPN phase 1 (IKEv2, AES-256, SHA-384, DH group 20, certificates)"; FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, "config vpn ipsec phase1-interface"

Prerequisite: A PKI peer user that names the trusted CA and the expected certificate subject
What it enables: IPsec certificate authentication that accepts only the intended peer
How to put it in place: config user peer; edit <PEER_USER>; set ca <CA_CERT>; set subject <SUBJECT>; next; end
Source: Chapter row "PKI peer users for certificate authentication"; FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, "config user peer"

Prerequisite: The neighboring routers configured with the same authentication keys and key lifetimes, and the key chain defined on the FortiGate
What it enables: Authenticated OSPF and BGP adjacencies
How to put it in place: Agree on the keys with the neighbors' administrators; key chain: config router key-chain; edit <KEYCHAIN>; config key; edit 1; set key-string <KEY>; set algorithm hmac-sha256; next; end; next; end
Source: Chapter rows "Key chains for routing protocol authentication" and "BGP neighbors (passwords, maximum prefixes, inbound prefix lists)"; FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, "config router key-chain"

Prerequisite: A firewall policy (or proxy policy) that matches the traffic and applies the security profile, with proxy-based inspection for proxy-mode features
What it enables: Security profile settings, which take effect only on the traffic of a policy that uses them
How to put it in place: config firewall policy; edit <POLICY_ID>; set inspection-mode proxy; set utm-status enable; next; end (proxy mode only where the feature needs it); or GUI: Policy & Objects > Firewall Policy
Source: FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, "config firewall policy" (inspection-mode, utm-status); FortiOS 7.4.0 NFG, "Add inline CASB security profile" (a firewall policy must use proxy-based inspection)
